turns.en: Okay. The phone did not arrive here, so let's take then the question in the back.
turns.zh: 好的。手机没有到这里，那么让我们回答后面的问题。

turns.en: So, first of all, thank you very much for becoming here. And in Vienna we say "Herzlich willkommen." So, my question is you were talking about that AI was like a baby. And but it was like it was my baby.
turns.zh: 首先，非常感谢您来到这里。在维也纳我们说“Herzlich willkommen”。那么，我的问题是，您谈到人工智能就像婴儿。但就像它是我的婴儿。

turns.en: No, no. We're like the baby. AI is like our mother.
turns.zh: 不，不。我们像婴儿。人工智能像我们的母亲。

turns.en: I think we are training the AI. And my question is, should we start having like rules who are allowed to starting to train AI? Just to be safe.
turns.zh: 我认为我们在训练人工智能。我的问题是，我们是否应该开始制定规则，规定谁被允许开始训练人工智能？只是为了安全。

turns.en: That's not a bad idea. I mean, for example, I think training AI to predict the next word in an uncurated corpus of all the documents on the web you can get your hands on is actually training it to be able to adopt all sorts of different personalities, the personality of a psychopath and so on. Or a mega supporter. And I didn't think that's a good way to train something. I mean, they're willing to train it on the diaries of serial killers as far as I know. You wouldn't teach your kid to read on those. My belief is we ought to be training AIs on highly curated data that exhibits very good behavior. The kind of behavior we'd like the AIs to exhibit later in life. And we should never show it bad behavior until it's learned enough about good behavior to recognize that is bad behavior. What we do now is we show it a mix of everything. And that's great for training it to be good at prediction.
turns.zh: 这不是个坏主意。我的意思是，例如，我认为训练人工智能在你能获取的网络上所有文档的未整理语料库中预测下一个词，实际上是在训练它能够采用各种不同的人格，精神病患者的人格等等。或者一个超级支持者。我不认为这是训练某物的好方法。我的意思是，据我所知，他们愿意用连环杀手的日记来训练它。你不会教你的孩子读那些。我的信念是，我们应该用高度整理的数据来训练人工智能，这些数据表现出非常好的行为。我们希望人工智能在以后生活中表现出的那种行为。我们不应该向它展示坏行为，直到它学到了足够多的好行为，能够认识到那是坏行为。我们现在做的是向它展示一切的混合。这对于训练它擅长预测很好。

turns.en: But you've now trained something that has all these different personalities it can take on, knows how to do good things, knows how to do bad things, doesn't really know the difference between good and bad. That's not a good way to do business. I think it should be much more curated. And maybe you should need a license to train an AI, because we don't want people training it on bad stuff.
turns.zh: 但你现在训练出来的东西拥有各种可以扮演的人格，知道怎么做好事，也知道怎么做坏事，却并不真正分得清好与坏。这不是一种好的做事方式。我认为它应该受到更多的筛选和管控。也许训练 AI 应该需要许可证，因为我们不希望人们用坏东西来训练它。

turns.en: Okay, maybe an online question and then a question over here. So I'm summarizing some of the online questions. One of them is: you quit Google to talk more openly about AI risks. Can you walk us through the process that led there? You started there some 10 years ago. What were the key events that made you change your mind?
turns.zh: 好，也许先问一个线上的问题，然后再问这边的问题。我在汇总一些线上提问。其中一个是：你离开 Google，是为了更公开地谈论 AI 风险。你能带我们梳理一下走到那一步的过程吗？你大约 10 年前开始在那里工作。有哪些关键事件让你改变了想法？

turns.en: Okay, there were two things that happened at more or less the same time, within a year of one another. Google already had chatbots before ChatGPT that could explain to you why a joke was funny. And I'd always had that in the back of my mind as a criterion for real understanding. If an AI really understood language, it should be able to explain why a joke's funny. And Google had a chatbot called Palm that could do that. So that made me believe, yes, they really do understand. They're not just faking it. They really do understand.
turns.zh: 好，有两件事几乎同时发生，前后相差不到一年。在 ChatGPT 之前，Google 就已经有聊天机器人能向你解释一个笑话为什么好笑。我一直把这一点默默当作真正理解的标准。如果一个 AI 真正理解了语言，它就应该能解释一个笑话为什么好笑。Google 有一个叫 Palm 的聊天机器人能做到这一点。所以这让我相信，是的，它们真的理解了。它们不只是假装。它们真的理解了。

turns.en: And then at a similar time, I was working on figuring out whether you'd be able to make analog large language models, and understanding why you couldn't, or understanding the big advantage of the digital ones, which is they can share information so well. And that combination — they really understand language and they can share billions of times better than we can — started making me think, wow, maybe this is a much better form of intelligence that's going to replace us. And that was in early 2023. And so a few months later, I left Google.
turns.zh: 然后在差不多同一时期，我在研究能否做出模拟式的大语言模型，并弄明白为什么做不成，或者说弄明白数字模型的巨大优势，就是它们能如此出色地共享信息。这两点结合起来——它们真正理解语言，而且共享信息的能力比我们强几十亿倍——开始让我想，哇，也许这是一种好得多的智能形式，将会取代我们。那是 2023 年初。所以几个月后，我离开了 Google。

turns.en: Now, I should say I left Google because I wanted to retire and watch more Netflix, and I couldn't program anymore because I kept forgetting the names of the variables. I took the opportunity to warn about the risks of AI. But there's a story in the media which is a much better story, which is that this noble guy gave up his huge Google salary so he could warn about the risks of AI. It's complete nonsense, but don't let me stop you propagating it.
turns.zh: 不过我得说明，我离开 Google 是因为我想退休、多看些 Netflix，而且我没法再编程了，因为我老是忘记变量的名字。我借这个机会警告 AI 的风险。但媒体上有一个故事，那个故事要好听得多，说的是这位高尚的人放弃了他在 Google 的高薪，以便警告 AI 的风险。这完全是胡说八道，但我不拦着你们继续传播它。

turns.en: You painted this powerful picture of AI working or acting like a mother. Maybe a smart mother. But you said now everyone is training AI to be smart. Could there be a point of no return where AI is being trained smart and you cannot change it anymore to being a smart mother?
turns.zh: 你描绘了一幅很有力的图景：AI 像母亲一样运作或行事。也许是一位聪明的母亲。但你说现在所有人都在把 AI 训练得聪明。会不会出现一个不可回头的临界点，AI 已经被训练得很聪明，你就再也无法把它改成一位聪明的母亲了？

turns.en: Not if we're still free to change how we train it. But if AI takes over, that's the point of no return. If AI takes over from people and we're just relegated to running the power stations, I don't think there's a way back from that. AI would have incredible control because of all the surveillance it could do and so on. It's not like a computer game where you say, okay, didn't work that time, let's try again. We've got to get this right the first time, which is a bit worrying.
turns.zh: 只要我们还能自由地改变训练方式，就不会。但如果 AI 接管了，那就是不可回头的临界点。如果 AI 从人类手中接管，而我们只是被降级去运行发电站，我认为那就没有回头路了。AI 会拥有惊人的控制力，因为它能进行各种监控等等。这不像电脑游戏，你可以说，好吧，那次没成功，再试一次。我们必须在第一次就做对，这有点令人担忧。

turns.en: Yeah, I think we should take a few more questions, two or three questions, all right?
turns.zh: 是的，我想我们应该再回答几个问题，两三个问题，好吗？

turns.en: I'm happy.
turns.zh: 我很乐意。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Can I be next? Sorry. Sorry, you. One last quick question. What is consciousness in your opinion? Could you answer this intuitively, please?
turns.zh: 我能下一个吗？抱歉。抱歉，你先。最后一个快问。在你看来，意识是什么？请凭直觉回答一下，好吗？

turns.en: Okay. I think I've already explained what I think subjective experience is, and it's not an inner thing. Subjective experience is a way of talking about counterfactual after-effects that would explain how our perception's gone wrong. I think the best thing I can do to give you an idea of what I think about consciousness is explain a bit more about perception.
turns.zh: 好。我想我已经解释过我认为的主观体验是什么，它不是一种内在的东西。主观体验是一种谈论反事实后效的方式，这些后效能解释我们的感知是如何出错的。我想，要让你了解我对意识的看法，最好的办法是多解释一点感知。

turns.en: So let's suppose there's an apple on the table, because philosophers like apples. There's an apple on the table in front of me, and most people would think that what happens is light rays from the apple come onto my retina, I get an upside-down image of the apple, then there's various stages of processing in my brain, and then somehow there's this thing in my mind which is the thing I actually experience as the experience of the apple. I don't think it's like that at all.
turns.zh: 假设桌上有一个苹果，因为哲学家喜欢苹果。我面前的桌上有一个苹果，大多数人会认为发生的过程是：来自苹果的光线落到我的视网膜上，我得到一个倒立的苹果图像，然后大脑里有各个阶段的处理，接着不知怎么地，我心中就有了一样东西，那才是我实际体验到的、对苹果的体验。我完全不认为是这样。

turns.en: I think what happens is there's an apple there, and if my perception's working normally, I experience the apple. What I experience is the thing in the world, the physical thing in the world. That's what I experience. In order to experience it, I have to have the image on my retina, I have to have the various stages of processing in my brain, but that's how I experience the apple. It's not that there's a thing inside that I experience. It's the apple I experience.
turns.zh: 我认为发生的是：那里有一个苹果，如果我的感知正常运作，我就体验到那个苹果。我体验到的是世界中的那个东西，世界中的那个物理对象。那才是我体验到的。为了体验到它，我必须让图像落在视网膜上，必须让大脑进行各个阶段的处理，但那就是我体验苹果的方式。并不是我内心有一样东西被我体验到，我体验到的是那个苹果。

turns.en: You may not see right now why that's relevant to consciousness, but I think it's part of the story that the whole concept of there being an inner world just isn't one.
turns.zh: 你现在可能看不出这跟意识有什么关系，但我认为这是整个说法的一部分：所谓存在一个内在世界，这个概念本身就不成立。

turns.en: Okay, please.
turns.zh: 好，请。

turns.en: Thank you very much. You mentioned two species. One with the tigers and we extincted them nearly totally already, and the chicken we put them into cages and some are running around in the meadows. I really have problems with this mother-baby metaphor. I cannot imagine how that works out. So, is there — as we remain the chicken and not being extinct like the tiger — can we make ourselves somehow useful to the AI in the future?
turns.zh: 非常感谢。你提到了两个物种。一个是老虎，我们几乎已经把它们灭绝了；另一个是鸡，我们把它们关进笼子，还有一些在草地上跑来跑去。我真的对这个母亲—婴儿的比喻有疑问。我无法想象那会怎样实现。那么，如果我们继续做鸡、而不是像老虎那样灭绝，我们能不能在未来以某种方式让自己对 AI 有用？

turns.en: Sorry, make ourselves useful to the AIs?
turns.zh: 抱歉，让自己对 AI 有用？

turns.en: The AIs, sir.
turns.zh: 对 AI，先生。

turns.en: Well, we're useful to the AIs by running the power stations. But if the AIs are much smarter than us, I think we're going to be slaves to the AIs. When they're smarter than us, I think our only hope is we've designed them so they care more about us than about themselves. That's my belief.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们通过运行发电站来对 AI 有用。但如果 AI 比我们聪明得多，我认为我们会成为 AI 的奴隶。当它们比我们聪明时，我认为我们唯一的希望是：我们把它们设计成关心我们胜过关心它们自己。这是我的信念。

turns.en: Now, there's many other people working on AI safety and I also believe very strongly we should adopt — try many different approaches. This is a kind of life or death thing and it'd be stupid to focus on one approach. We should put lots of research money — if you've been an academic for many years, your main goal in life is to get more research money, and I can't stop it now just because I don't need the research money. We should put lots of research funding into all the different ways in which we might happily coexist with AI. And the sort of baby-mother relationship is one possibility, but we should be exploring lots of others as well.
turns.zh: 现在有很多其他人在研究 AI 安全，我也非常坚信我们应该采纳——尝试许多不同的方法。这多少是生死攸关的事，只专注于一种方法会很愚蠢。我们应该投入大量研究经费——如果你做了多年学者，你人生的主要目标就是拿到更多研究经费，我不能因为自己现在不需要研究经费就停下来。我们应该把大量研究经费投入到我们可能与 AI 愉快共存的种种不同方式中。那种婴儿—母亲的关系是一种可能，但我们也应该探索许多其他可能。

turns.en: Okay, maybe a last online question and yeah, there are so many questions, but I think we can't answer all.
turns.zh: 好，也许最后一个线上问题，是的，问题太多了，但我想我们没法全部回答。

turns.en: Okay, so we've obviously got a lot of students here and also watching from the other rooms. So a highly popular question here is: in these times of uncertainty, what would be your advice for young scientists at the beginning of their career? What should they do?
turns.zh: 好，我们这里显然有很多学生，还有其他房间在观看的学生。这里一个非常受欢迎的问题是：在这个充满不确定性的时代，你对刚起步的年轻科学家有什么建议？他们应该怎么做？

turns.en: Yeah, I wish I had some kind of good advice for them.
turns.zh: 是啊，我希望我能给他们一些好的建议。

turns.en: The best advice I have is learn a certain amount of STEM so you understand at least what's going on in AI. But also get a good education that teaches you to think for yourself. That's the best I can offer. Also maybe learn to do plumbing, just in case.
turns.zh: 我能给的最好的建议是，学一些 STEM 的东西，这样你至少能理解 AI 领域在发生什么。但也要接受良好的教育，学会独立思考。这是我能给出的最好的建议。另外，也许可以学学水管工，以防万一。

turns.en: Okay, I think let's please stay here. Let's make an applause for Geoffrey. And I hand over to Gerti Kappel, the Dean of the Faculty of Informatics.
turns.zh: 好，我想请大家先留在这里。让我们为 Geoffrey 鼓掌。接下来我把话筒交给信息学系主任 Gerti Kappel。

turns.en: This works. Thank you very much for your presentation. Just two sentences. Our rector was mentioning enlightenment — you know, 100 years ago there was the Wiener Kreis, the philosophers, the mathematicians, the logicians who tried to change the world. Unfortunately, it didn't work out at that time, but something like 100 years later in this house, there was the movement of the digital humanism initiative started here six or seven years ago. And there's the book on introduction to digital humanism. So perhaps next time, I think we're on the same page, you will talk about digital humanism.
turns.zh: 这样就行了。非常感谢您的演讲。我只说两句。我们的校长刚才提到了启蒙——你知道，100 年前有维也纳学派，那些哲学家、数学家、逻辑学家试图改变世界。遗憾的是，当时没能成功，但大约 100 年后，就在这栋楼里，数字人文主义倡议的运动六七年前在这里发起。还有一本关于数字人文主义导论的书。所以也许下一次，我想我们想法一致，您会谈谈数字人文主义。

turns.en: Thank you very much.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。

turns.en: And you know, the brain only works if you have something to eat, and we have learned that he really likes very good, very healthy food like Manner cookies and there are the Mozart balls. So, we have a full souvenir bag of sweets for you.
turns.zh: 你知道，大脑只有吃饱了才能运转，我们了解到他特别喜欢非常好、非常健康的食物，比如 Manner 饼干，还有莫扎特巧克力球。所以我们为您准备了一整袋糖果纪念品。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.en: So, the last part, which is the informal get-together on the third floor, is open now. Don't go away. Stay on the third floor and continue discussing. Thank you.
turns.zh: 那么最后一部分，也就是三楼的非正式交流会，现在开放了。别走开。请留在三楼继续讨论。谢谢。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

tldr.en: LLMs understand language by finding compatible feature vectors, much like humans.
tldr.zh: 大语言模型通过寻找兼容的特征向量来理解语言，这与人类非常相似。

tldr.en: Digital intelligence can share knowledge billions of times faster than humans via weight sharing.
tldr.zh: 数字智能可以通过权重共享以比人类快数十亿倍的速度分享知识。

tldr.en: We should design AI to care about humans more than itself, like a mother for a baby.
tldr.zh: 我们应该设计 AI 像母亲对待婴儿一样，关心人类胜过关心自己。
